text: sake example, ’ll simulate tiny repository. [!NOTE] Typically ’d combine repository package metadata package source like CRAN. Since ’re simulating fake packages, ’ll use metric package repositories. Use package_filter() limit high quality packages. example enforce trivial policy, requiring packages checked without error ’re top 75% packages number downloads. can inspect package database see now point Repository called <filtered>. ’re still , ’d fail install real repository url. Let’s see happens try install anyways!
code: library(val.criterion) library(val.meter) repo <- val.meter::random_repo(n = 10) options(   repos = repo,  # for the sake of example   val.criterion.repos = repo,   available_packages_filters = package_filter({     r_cmd_check_error_count == 0 &       percentile(downloads_total) >= 0.25   }) ) # grab the first package that was disallowed by our filter pkgs <- as.data.frame(available.packages()) filtered_pkg <- subset(pkgs, Repository == "<filtered>")$Package[[1L]] #> ℹ excluding 3 packages according to package filtering policy install.packages(filtered_pkg) #> Installing package into ‘/usr/local/lib/R/site-library’ #> (as ‘lib’ is unspecified) #> Error in `install.packages()`: #> ! required packages are excluded due to package filters #> "admirr" #> ℹ To explain, use `val.criterion::last_rejected()` #> ℹ To permit exceptions, use `val.criterion::last_rejected_permit()` #> Run `rlang::last_trace()` to see where the error occurred.

title: Options As Parameters — options_params
text: quiet Wether filtering operations reported queried. Passed quiet parameter individual functions used. (Defaults FALSE, overwritable using option 'val.criterion.quiet' environment variable 'R_VAL_CRITERION_QUIET') repos Metrics repositories use implicitly package filters. accessed using available.packages(), repository paths follow similar conventions. (Defaults character(0L), overwritable using option 'val.criterion.repos' environment variable 'R_VAL_CRITERION_REPOS') exceptions Packages treated exceptions. Even otherwise filtered using preset filters, still discoverable installable without issue. (Defaults character(0L), overwritable using option 'val.criterion.exceptions' environment variable 'R_VAL_CRITERION_EXCEPTIONS') actions set calls prompt actions. See default_actions example expected format. (Defaults default_actions(), overwritable using option 'val.criterion.actions' environment variable 'R_VAL_CRITERION_ACTIONS')

code: if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ library(val.meter)  # simulate repository of metrics, mirroring existing available packages repo <- val.meter::random_repo(n = 10) options(   repos = repo,  # for the sake of example   val.criterion.repos = repo,   available_packages_filters = package_filter({     r_cmd_check_error_count == 0 &       percentile(downloads_total) >= 0.25   }) )  # grab the first package that was disallowed by our filter pkgs <- available.packages() filtered_pkg <- pkgs[pkgs$Repository == "<filtered>", ][[1L]]  # attempt to install it install.packages(filtered_pkg) } # }
